items.h: Set for expanded role with Addison out again
items.s: Felton is poised to maintain an expanded role Sunday against the Falcons, as Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports that Jordan Addison (thumb) will remain sidelined. Felton stepped up in Addison's absence during the Week 11 loss to San Francisco, leading the Vikings with 12 targets en route to six catches for 42 yards. Jauan Jennings and Myles Price also are candidates for additional targets from Kirk Cousins behind Justin Jefferson against a Falcons defense that gives up the fifth-most passing yards per game.

Felton (hip) was listed as a full participant on Thursday's injury report. Felton was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough by a hip injury, but his ability to get back to full one day later gives him the all clear for Sunday's game versus the Falcons. Assuming Jordan Addison (thumb) misses a third consecutive contest in Week 12, Felton again will be a candidate for an expanded role, which has translated to nine catches (on 17 targets) for 75 yards the last two outings.

Felton (hip) was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough. Felton has had increased sway in the Vikings offense the past two games with Jordan Addison sidelined, combining for nine catches (on 17 targets) for 75 yards. Addison is trending toward another absence Sunday against the Falcons, so Felton is in line to continue his elevated role this weekend, assuming he's able to play through his hip injury.

items.h: Tai Felton Is a Week 12 PPR Fill-In
items.s: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton is worth a small Week 12 claim in 14-team full-PPR leagues if you need a flex. Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday that Jordan Addison (thumb) is unlikely to return for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons. Felton caught six passes for 42 yards on a team-high 12 targets in the loss to the San Francisco 49ers, with six of those targets coming in the first half. Minnesota threw 43 passes in the blowout after attempting 31 in the win over the Green Bay Packers. Felton drew five targets at Green Bay despite playing more snaps. Jauan Jennings returned from a calf injury against San Francisco and played more than Felton, leaving the two to share…

items.h: Tai Felton catches six passes in Week 11 loss
items.s: Tai Felton brought in 6-of-12 targets for 42 yards in Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. Felton saw a team-high 12 targets Sunday night, as the second-year pro has been more involved in the offense with Jordan Addison out (thumb) out the past couple of weeks. Felton was limited in his yardage and only came up with half of the tosses that came his way, but he does merit PPR consideration while Addison remains out.

Felton caught six of 12 targets for 42 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. Felton was set to operate in an expanded role with Jordan Addison (thumb) on injured reserve, and he garnered a game-high 12 targets. The wide receiver finished tied for second on the team in catches with tight end T.J. Hockenson while fellow wideout Justin Jefferson (seven) led the way. Felton has caught nine of 17 targets for 75 yards over the last two weeks, and his next chance to build off of his recent momentum will come in Week 12 against the Falcons.

items.h: Tai Felton sees five targets in Week 10 win
items.s: Tai Felton caught three of his five targets for 33 yards in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10. Felton has struggled to make an impact in the Minnesota offense to this point, recording under 35 receiving yards in each of his nine contests. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 11 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports. Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

items.h: Light playing time again in Week 9
items.s: Felton went without a target while playing six of the Vikings' 48 offensive snaps in Monday's 23-6 loss to the Bills. Felton continues to handle a muted role as a depth receiver for Minnesota, as Monday marked the third consecutive game in which he played single-digit snaps. For the season, the second-year wideout out of Maryland has been limited to just three receptions for 41 yards on seven targets over eight appearances.

Tai Felton caught two of his three targets for 27 yards in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the New Orleans Saints in Week 5. Felton has been minimally involved in the Minnesota offense to begin the season, finishing under 30 receiving yards in each of the first five games. The wideout can remain off rosters in all formats as the team enters a Week 6 bye.

items.h: Tai Felton to Have Larger Role with Jefferson Out
items.s: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton is expected to see a larger role in Week 4 against the Miami Dolphins. Star wideout Justin Jefferson suffered an ankle sprain that has ruled him out, leaving Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, and Felton as the receivers with significant roles. The second-year receiver had two targets but no receptions in the 23-16 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, yet he played 55% of the snaps and 65% of the routes after Jefferson left the game early. He faces a Dolphins defense that has allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy points to wide receivers this season, but also the seventh-most passing yards. With a limited role behind Addison and Jennings still expected,…

items.h: Tai Felton Remains Without Legitimate Role
items.s: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton has done nothing to contribute in the passing game yet. In fact, Felton has only played five percent of the offensive snaps during the first two games of the season. Barring any injuries, Felton is unlikely to have much of a role at all in the passing attack this season. The Vikings brought in Jauan Jennings this offseason to be the third wideout behind Jordan Addison and Justin Jefferson. The second-year wideout has no clear path to playing on this roster right now. There's some dynasty stash value because one injury could move him into a starting role, but Felton is unlikely to do anything until then.

items.h: Tai Felton Has Strong Day Against Ravens
items.s: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton hauled in three of four targets for 66 yards in the 13-3 preseason loss to the Baltimore Ravens. Felton caught a 50-yard bomb from quarterback J.J. McCarthy down the right sideline, headlining a strong day for the second-year receiver. With the three starting receivers, Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings, all sitting out, Felton was the lead receiver. He played 18 of 19 snaps, ran 11 routes, and led the starting offense in targets against the Ravens. Some have speculated that Felton could be the WR3, ahead of Jennings in the receiver rotation, and Saturday's strong outing lends credibility to those theories. While Felton is…

items.h: Tai Felton a Top Performer in Camp, Pushing for WR3 Role
items.s: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Tai Felton has been one of the team's top performers this training camp, according to ESPN's Kevin Seifert. Felton was a third-round pick out of Maryland before last season but only had three catches for 25 yards in his rookie season, contributing mostly on special teams. This season, though, he has been pushing newly acquired Jauan Jennings for playing time with an outstanding training camp, earning praise for his route-running and winning contested catches in the red zone and in the open field. Felton is still a deep-league sleeper at this point, but he's definitely a name to watch since the Vikings' passing game could get a boost with Kyler Murray…
